criteria.error_taxonomy: Malformed, expired and mismatched tokens each fail a dedicated domain error, keeping causes distinguishable to callers.
criteria.false_all: False is the single answer for token faults and configuration faults together, with no domain errors from verify.
criteria.false_vs_config: False covers token faults (malformed, expired, wrong session, wrong secret); domain errors cover configuration faults (empty secret, empty session, out-of-range durations).

csrf_failure.instructions: What should callers observe from each class of CSRF failure?

criteria.all_pairs: Return all pairs for the name in arrival order and let the caller choose among them.
criteria.first_wins: Return the opening pair for the name per the native getter and also expose the arrival-ordered pair list.
criteria.last_wins: Return the closing pair for the name so trailing entries override leading entries.

duplicates.instructions: When a request repeats a cookie name, which entry wins lookup?

criteria.adapter_enforces: Refuse prefix violations (__Host- without Secure with Path=/ and absent Domain; __Secure- without Secure) and insecure SameSite=None as domain errors ahead of serialization.
criteria.enforce_prefix_only: Refuse prefix violations in the adapter while SameSite combinations serialize natively.
criteria.serialize_native: Serialize the native-accepted attribute set and record browser consequences in prose; enforce nothing further.

policy.instructions: Does prefix and SameSite enforcement belong in the adapter?

criteria.default_secret: Permit the native restart-volatile thread default when callers pass no secret.
criteria.explicit_required: Demand caller secrets and nonempty sessions on all operations; offer no defaulting.
criteria.secret_handle: Issue opaque secret handles and forbid raw secret strings at the boundary, paralleling crypto keys.

secret.instructions: Which credential form do CSRF operations accept?

state: Can emits TypeScript pinned to Bun 1.4.2 (bun-1.4.2-darwin-arm64-v1, revision 744846f844374847c902b5e7fd59b4342a51ef99). B1-09 contributes typed cookies plus session-bound CSRF above HTTP (B1-06) and crypto (B1-08). The pinned ledger shows: CookieMap stores repeated pairs in arrival order but lookup takes the opening entry (first-wins), and JSON output keeps the opening entry too; name casing matters; '='-less fragments and nameless entries disappear; valueless entries keep blank strings; outer padding strips; quotation neither escapes inner semicolons nor removes quotes; value escapes percent-decode; cutting uses the first '='; unknown names give null on get and false on has. Bun.Cookie assumes Path=/ and SameSite=Lax, printing each every time; SameSite=None sans Secure prints flagless; unknown sameSite throws TypeError; CRLF, semicolons, spaces, '=' and empty strings throw TypeError as names whereas commas pass; CRLF, semicolons and unicode percent-encode as values; __Host- and __Secure- print with unrestricted attributes (prefix rules unenforced); negative maxAge prints literally; zero maxAge and bygone expiry count expired. Map removal prints blank epoch-expiry entries preserving the supplied domain and path; getSetCookie keeps repeated entries apart while plain get fuses them with commas. CSRF mints 86-character strings, unique per call; checking yields false on foreign sessions, foreign secrets, junk, shortened and tampered tokens; session linkage holds firmly in both directions; empty sessionId, empty secret and non-string tokens throw TypeError; optionless checks yield false; the thread-scoped fallback secret validates its own mintings; token expiry overrules maxAge entirely; zero maxAge still validates mint-fresh tokens, yet negative or enormous maxAge and negative expiresIn throw RangeError. Layout stays fixed: runtime/platform/cookies.ts with csrf.ts implement the adapters, http.ts retains repeated Set-Cookie entries distinctly, emit/runtime_cookies.go binds both. Adapters emit the Completion form with source origin under declared error limits. Assertions avoid whole random-token comparisons; cookie mappings run for real; session sourcing and unsafe-request gating are application concerns.
